packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-15 - blind image reading (unverified)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading. Beyond the rules: I ran `ls` on the packet directory itself and `sips` to get image pixel sizes (no contents of packet.json or any other directory were read).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of face 1)
- Object: a small fragment made of narrow vertical parchment strips (binding strips / cut slips), upright orientation, mounted under a strip of brown paper/tape across the top which carries a pencil shelfmark-like note (not read for content). About 11 cm tall, ~11 cm wide overall.
- Left: one separate narrow strip (approx. 2.5 cm wide), ~22-23 written lines visible.
- Right: a block of three or four adjoining strips (cut along vertical lines), text continues across cuts in places; appears to be one or two columns of a small-format text cut into strips.
- Script: small gothic textualis, heavily abbreviated, closely written; frequent paragraph marks alternating red and blue (pilcrows), no enlarged initials visible, no running title visible. Line count per strip ~22-24.
- Tentative: a densely abbreviated scholastic/legal-type prose text with paragraphus marks dividing sentences; no visible gloss or commentary arrangement.
- Tiles image-002..005 appear to be the native-resolution tiles of this face (2x2 grid, overlapping); image-006 is the overview of the other face with tiles 007..010.

FACE 1 TILES
image-002 (top-left tile): left strip lines 1-9 visible below the brown tape; right edge shows the left part of the right-hand strip block (first strip, faded/rubbed, lines 1-9).
Conventions: q; = q(ue); ' = abbreviation superscript; ¶ = paragraph mark (colour given).

Left strip (A), image-002:
002.A1  [.]nu(m)? q(ue) ãi cis? poti-   (first letters cut at left edge; "ãi" with macron, reading uncertain)
002.A2  c(?) xxlv? · c · [red ¶] Sed q(uod)?

002.A4  z (= et) qui excludu(n)t-?
002.A5  in addic(i)o(n)ib(us)   ("addiciõib9")
002.A6  tu n(un)c? p(ro)pt(er)? as ve-   ("nc" written superscript above "tu"; "pt" with bar)
002.A7  -ue gr(ati)e? d(i)c(t)as? sc(ilicet)?   ("gr̃e dcias sc")
002.A8  -ant · q · cxlvij? · c ·  (looks like a numbered citation: q(uestio)? c(apitulum)?)
002.A9  noua · e(t)? · q · a-   (line partly cut at bottom of tile)

Right block, first strip (B), image-002 (faded ink, left letters lost on cut edge):

image-003 (top-right tile): shows the brown tape with pencil note "Stams, STA, Frag. 150m" (modern mount label; transcribed only as seen). Below: right portion of strip B (overlaps image-002 B1-B9, not repeated), then strip C (middle) and strip D (right). Strips B, C, D are cut from one written area and text seems to run on across the cuts (e.g. C4 "Sus-" + D4 "pensio"), so B|C|D are probably adjacent pieces of one column; small losses at each cut.

Strip C, image-003:

003.C3  iudex? p(re)ce(n)te? / p(ro)cede(n)te?   ("udex pcẽte", reading uncertain)

003.D5  -nce? no(n) suspe(n)di-?   ("nc̃ nõ suspẽdi")
003.D6  [red ¶] Sub q(ui)b(us) form(is)?   ("Subq; forms")

003.D9  [cut at bottom of tile]

Strip C left edge, image-004 (only first letters visible; read on image-005 if possible): "-io", "aliu-", "qui", "inith-?", "-is icas?", "· e · [blue ¶]".

005.12  -am? i(n) aggrauac(i)o(n)e(m)? | c(on)firmac(i)o(n)is? ad-   (uncertain: "cõſ'macõis")

Note: the numerals after "q ·" recur through the face (cxlvij?, cxxxvij?, cxxxvi?) followed by "c" or "e"; they look like paragraph-end reference marks (number + letter), but I cannot settle the numerals reliably at this scale.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-006, overview of face 2 = reverse; mount label reads "Stams, STA, Frag. 150v")
- Mirror arrangement of face 1: here the block of three adjoining strips is at left and the single narrow strip at right (consistent with the object being turned over).
- Left block: three strips, ~22 lines each, ink in places rubbed/faded (left and middle strips), dark in the third strip; red and blue paragraph marks as on face 1. Right single strip: ~22 lines, red and blue paragraph marks.
- Same small gothic textualis; no headings, initials or glosses visible.
- Tiles 007 (top-left), 008 (top-right), 009 (bottom-left), 010 (bottom-right) assumed.

FACE 2 TILES

Text appears to continue across the cuts (e.g. F3 "al-" | G3 "-iquo"; F5? | G?), so E|F|G are adjacent pieces of one column. Ink of E and F is browner and partly rubbed.
